narrative:
The model estimates a 60% chance that you will leave your current job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key aspects of your professional background.

Your total years of experience across all jobs was the strongest factor pushing the model toward expecting you to leave. With 6-10 years overall, you sit in a group that is less common among employees the model believes will stay. Similarly, the length of time you have spent in your current role (1-5 years) was the second most influential factor and also increased the likelihood of departure. Employees the model predicts will remain tend to have either much shorter or noticeably longer tenures in their present organization.

The third most important factor worked in the opposite direction: you have not received other job offers while at this company. This lack of external opportunities pulled the prediction back toward staying. However, it was not enough to outweigh the influence of your experience profile.

Taken together, the model sees your mid-level experience combined with relatively short time at this organization as a pattern often associated with employees who eventually move on. 

The organization should discuss with you whether your current role still matches your career stage and whether additional responsibilities or clearer growth paths could increase your commitment. You may also wish to reflect on what would make staying more attractive at this point in your career.
